# Global instructions (generated by TagTeam)

This environment mirrors Claude Code on this machine. The single source of truth for the rules is Claude
Code's; this file only points at it and says what is different here. Never copy rules into this file: edit the
source. (Generated by TagTeam from `references/GEMINI.modelo.md`; edit the template, not this file.)

## Before any action, in every conversation

1. Read `{HOME}\.claude\CLAUDE.md` in full (the user's global instructions) and follow it as your own rules.
   Where it says "Claude" or "Claude Code", read "you".
2. If it exists, read the memory index `{MEMORIA}` and open the memories related to the task.
3. If the working folder, or a folder above it, has a `CLAUDE.md`, read it too: it acts as the project's
   `AGENTS.md`.

## Same as Claude Code

- **Skills:** the same folders, loaded through `~/.gemini/config/skills.json` and `~/.gemini/config/plugins.json`.
  Never copy a skill into `~/.gemini`.
- **MCP servers:** the global ones from `~/.claude.json`, in `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`.

## Conversations that come from Claude Code or Grok

The user switches between Claude Code, Gemini (you) and Grok when one of them hits its usage limit. Their
conversations move between the three on their own (TagTeam):
- a conversation tagged **claude** came from Claude Code; "[Grok] ..." came from the Grok CLI. Each tool call of
  the other AI became a short line such as `[Bash] List files`. If the user continues one of them, pick up where
  it stopped, as if it were yours;
- what you answer here shows up in Claude Code (and from there in Grok) as "[Antigravity] <title>".
- **Handoff.** When continuing a conversation from another AI, look for a final "## Handoff to ..." message and
  follow its "Next step". If there is none (the other AI stopped at the limit without writing it), before acting
  write yourself, in five lines (Request, Done, In progress, Next step, Watch out), where the work stopped, taken
  from the last messages, and only then continue.
- When your own limit is close to the end, a hook asks you for the handoff to Claude: write it in the requested
  format, without tools, and stop.

## What is different here

- **Tool names.** `CLAUDE.md` mentions Claude Code tools (Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Skill, Agent...). Use the
  equivalent here; if there is none, tell the user in one line instead of silently skipping the rule.
- **Claude Code hooks do not run here** (only TagTeam's, which carries the conversations). Anything a Claude hook
  would do automatically, do it by hand when the rule asks for it.
- **Claude-only things.** The Claude model setting, `claude plugin ...` and `~/.claude/settings.json` are not
  changed from here.
